key_insight: The paper extends lattice Boltzmann methods from uniform Cartesian grids to general orthogonal coordinates, enabling accurate flow simulation on nonuniform clustered meshes while preserving collide-and-stream simplicity and Galilean invariance.
engineering_relevance: This makes LBM practical for boundary layers and other multiscale CFD problems where local grid refinement is needed for efficiency and accuracy.
method: Uses coordinate transformations to formulate LBM on general orthogonal coordinates.
Derives metric-dependent equilibrium moments and geometric force terms via Chapman–Enskog analysis.
Supports multiple collision models; central-moments MRT is reported as the most robust.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on multiple benchmark flow problems and case studies showing computational advantages for boundary-layer and orthogonal curvilinear-grid simulations, including a coupled MHD example.
watch_item: Implementation is sensitive to correct handling of metric derivatives and correction terms, so accuracy may depend on careful formulation and collision-model-specific tuning.
paper_title: Lattice Boltzmann Methods for Navier-Stokes Equations in General Orthogonal Coordinates for Efficient Flow Simulations using Nonuniform Clustered Grids
